ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r8.claim: The object is fronted because it is the focus of rejection, not to claim exclusivity; the rejected act is seeking a religion other than God's.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r8.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لأنه المقصود بالانكار لا للحصر كما توهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan says fronting reflects looseness in expression and resemblance to the verse ending; al-Alusi says this explanation has no merit among careful scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r9.anchor: إن تعليل التقديم بما تقدم لا تحقيق فيه لأن الانكار الذي هو معنى الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r10.claim: Abu Amr, Hafs from Asim, and Yaqub read in the third person; the rest read in the second person, with an implied do you turn away, act impiously, or disbelieve, while some call it a shift of person.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية لحفص ويعقوب يبغون بالياء التحتية وقرأ الباقون بالتاء الفوقانية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r11.claim: The clause that all in the heavens and earth submit to Him is circumstantial and reinforces the rejection: how can they seek another religion in that state?
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r11.anchor: جملة حالية مؤكدة للانكار أي كيف يبغون ويطلبون غير دينه والحالة هذه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r12.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r12.claim: The two adverbs are circumstantial verbal nouns meaning willingly and unwillingly; Abu al-Baqa also treats them as verbal nouns for submission or obedience, though the source questions how that fits unwillingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r12.anchor: مصدران في موضع الحال أي طائعين وكارهين وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكونا مصدرين على غير المصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r13.claim: One reading takes willing submission as faith gained through knowledge, by reasoning or without reflection, and unwilling submission as Islam imposed by the sword or coercion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r13.anchor: المراد من الاسلام بالطوع الاسلام الناشي عن العلم مطلقا سواء كان حاصلا للاستدلال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r14.claim: Another reading says angels and believers obey willingly, while disbelievers are subject to God's will even in their disbelief; this does not entail determinism, erase their accountability, or collapse the distinction between believer and unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r14.anchor: انقادوا له تعالى مختارين لامره كالملائكة والمؤمنين مسخرين لارادته كالكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r15.speaker: بعض ساداتنا الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r15.claim: Sufi authorities distinguish willing submission without carnal darkness or ego veils from unwilling submission amid inner resistance, whispers, veils, and attachment to intermediaries.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r15.anchor: الاسلام طوعا هو الانقياد والامتثال لما أمر الله تعالى من غير معارضة ظلمة نفسانية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r16.claim: The Sufi account exemplifies the first state in angels and some elect people, and the second in many people who waver among religious schools without finding certainty, as the quoted poem illustrates.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r16.anchor: فلم أر إلا واضعا كف حائر على ذقن أو قارعا سن نادم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r17.claim: Unbelievers belong to the second class because they acknowledge a creator but their self-darkness prevents recognition of truth; the cited verses express that admission and their continued associationism.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r17.anchor: لانهم أثبتوا صانعا أيضا إلا أن ظلمة أنفسهم حالت بينهم وبين الوقوف على الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r18.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r18.claim: Al-Alusi says Mujahid's words point toward the Sufi account of the two kinds of submission.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r19.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r19.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says every person acknowledges God as Lord and self as servant; associating in worship is submission under compulsion, while sincere devotion is willing submission.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r20.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v3p212#3/r20.claim: Al-A'mash reads the word for unwillingly with a damma on its first consonant.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r1.claim: According to the well-known view, all return to God for recompense, so they should hasten to His religion and not oppose Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r1.anchor: أي إلى جزائه تصيرون على المشهور فبادروا إلى دينه ولا تخالفوا الاسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r2.claim: The return clause may stand independently as a threat or coordinate with all submit to Him as another circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r2.anchor: وجوزوا في الجملة أن تكون مستأنفة للاخبار بما تضمنته من التهديد وأن تكون معطوفة على ( وله أسلم )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r3.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r3.claim: Asim reads the return verb in the third person; its pronoun refers either to all who are in the heavens and earth or to those seeking another religion, with a person shift in the latter reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بياء الغيبة والضمير لمن أو لمن عاد اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r4.speaker: الباقون
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r4.claim: The other readers use the second person, with the pronoun returning to the people denoted by the subject of seeking; if the earlier verb is third person, this too creates a shift in person.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p214/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب والضمير عائد لمن عاد اليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.claim: The occasion was the People of the Book each claiming Abraham’s religion and disputing before the Prophet; when he said neither group followed Abraham’s religion, they rejected his judgment and religion, and the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.anchor: فادعى كل واحد أنه على دين إبراهيم عليه السلام واختصموا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, the Basrans, and Hafs from ʿAsim read the verb in the third person, matching the later reference to those who are defiantly disobedient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل البصرة وحفص عن عاصم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.claim: The other readers use the second person, matching the second person in the preceding address.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.claim: To submit here means to yield and comply.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.anchor: خضع وانقاد، {من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.claim: Willing submission is easy obedience; coerced submission involves difficulty and resistance of the self.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.anchor: فالطوع: الانقياد والاتباع بسهولة، والكره: ما كان بمشقة وإباء من النفس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the inhabitants of heaven submit willingly, while people on earth include willing believers and those compelled by fear of the sword and captivity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: أسلم أهل السموات طوعا وأسلم من في الأرض بعضهم طوعا وبعضهم كرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.claim: Mujahid identifies willing submission with the believer and coerced submission with the unbeliever, citing the verse that says all bow to God willingly or unwillingly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: طوعا المؤمن، وكرها ذلك الكافر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.claim: Another view places this submission at the primordial covenant, when people answered God’s question about His lordship, some willingly and some unwillingly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: هذا يوم الميثاق حين قال لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.claim: Qatada says the believer submits willingly and benefits, while the unbeliever’s coerced submission at the moment of danger is useless, as the verse about seeing punishment shows.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: المؤمن أسلم طوعا فنفعه، والكافر أسلم كرها في وقت البأس فلم ينفعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbi takes coerced submission as people calling sincerely upon God in distress, such as sailors in a storm.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.anchor: وقال الشعبي: هو استعاذتهم به عند اضطرارهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi says the willing are those born into Islam and the coerced are captives forced into Islam in chains.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.claim: Hafs from ʿAsim and Yaʿqub read the final verb in the third person; most use second person for both verbs, while Abu ʿAmr uses third person first and second person here because the first is specific and the return to God is universal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.anchor: قرأ بالياء حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r1.claim: The clause attaches to the preceding one, with the interrogative hamza inserted between them for denial; alternatively, supply “Do you turn away?” before “seek other than God’s religion?”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r1.anchor: عطف على الجملة المتقدمة والهمزة متوسطة بينهما للإنكار، أو محذوف تقديره أتتولون فغير دين الله تبغون

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r2.claim: The object is fronted because it is the focus of the denunciation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim in Ḥafṣ’s transmission, and Yaʿqūb read the verb in third person; the others read it in second person, understood as “and say to him.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r3.anchor: والفعل بلفظ الغيبة عند أبي عمرو وعاصم في رواية حفص ويعقوب، وبالتاء عند الباقين على تقدير وقل له

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r4.claim: Submission is voluntary through reflection and following proof, or compelled by force or signs that compel belief; alternatively, angels and believers submit willingly while unbelievers are subject to the decree and cannot resist it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r4.anchor: أي طائعين بالنظر واتباع الحجة، وكارهين بالسيف ومعاينة ما يلجىء إلى الإسلام كنتق الجبل وإدراك الغرق، والإشراف على الموت. أو مختارين كالملائكة والمؤمنين ومسخرين كالكفرة فإنهم لا يقدرون أن يمتنعوا عما قضى عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r5.claim: The verb is also read with yāʾ, with its pronoun referring back to “whoever.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:83/r5.anchor: وقرىء بالياء على أن الضمير لمن

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r1.claim: The verse closes the preceding accounts after God's testimony to Himself and the declaration that the religion with God is Islam, turning that context into rebuke and warning.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r1.anchor: خاتما لهذه القصص بعد الشهادة بنفسه المقدسة بما بدأها به في قوله { شهد الله } الآية إلى { إن الدين عند الله الإسلام }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r2.claim: An objection says fronting غير makes the rebuke target seeking exclusive status for another religion; the author answers that it foregrounds rejection, while exclusivity is considered after repudiating the other religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r2.anchor: بأن تقديمه الاهتمام بشأنه في الإنكار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r3.claim: God's religion is characterized by the attributes of perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r3.anchor: دين الله } الذي اختص بصفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r4.claim: He glosses يبغون as seeking through disobedience, or frames the phrase as أتوليتم on an address reading.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r5.claim: The phrase stresses that submission belongs exclusively to God.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r6.claim: Submission means obeying God's rulings and proceeding under His will and decree, which no one can overcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r6.anchor: خضع بالانقياد لأحكامة والجري تحت مراده وقضائه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r7.claim: Everyone in the heavens and earth submits, including those with bodily and intellectual power to defend themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r7.anchor: وهم من لهم قوة الدفاع بالبدن والعقل فكيف بغيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r8.claim: Voluntary submission is through faith or in what accords with people's interests.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r9.claim: Involuntary submission is submission to God's overpowering decree, even for the powerful with many allies, who remain helpless and unsupported.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r10.claim: They return to God at resurrection and will have no refuge, escape, or other destination.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r10.anchor: لا تعالجون مقرا ولا تلقون ملجأ ولا مفرا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r11.claim: Since no one can escape God's grasp by strength or stratagem in any state, resisting His command conveyed through messengers is untenable; miracles establish their messengership.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r11.anchor: فكيف يخالفون ما أتاهم من أمره على ألسنة رسله وقد ثبت أنهم رسله بما أتى به كل منهم من المعجزة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r12.claim: Defiance of a Messenger is defiance of the One who sent him.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p119#2/r12.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن المعاند للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم معاند للمرسل

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r6.claim: A report with a weak chain says those in heaven are angels, those on earth include people born Muslim, and the coerced are captives of nations led to Paradise in chains despite their reluctance.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r7.claim: Anas reports the Prophet explaining that angels obey God in heaven and the Ansar and Abd al-Qays obey him on earth.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r7.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says this submission occurred when God took the primordial covenant.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: حين أخذ الميثاق

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains submission as their collective worship of God and links the wording to the verse about all in heaven and earth prostrating willingly or unwillingly.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم من طريق علي عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: عبادتهم لي أجمعين

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r10.claim: Ikrima calls this phrase separate, then restates the wording about those in heaven and earth submitting willingly or unwillingly.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم من في السماوات} قال: هذه مفصولة

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses aslama as recognition or knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم} قال: المعرفة

DURR-FULL:v2p253/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r12.claim: Mujahid compares their submission to people's acknowledgment that God created the heavens and earth; that acknowledgment itself is their submission.
DURR-FULL:v2p253/r12.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن مجاهد في الآية قال: هو كقوله (ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله)

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every human acknowledged God as Lord and himself as God's servant: the polytheist submits unwillingly, while one who devotes worship to God submits willingly.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في الآية قال: كل آدمي أقر

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says some peoples were compelled to accept Islam while others came to it willingly.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الحسن في الآية قال: أكره أقوام على الإسلام وجاء أقوام طائعين

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r3.speaker: مطر الوراق
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r3.claim: Matar al-Warraq counts angels, the Ansar, Banu Sulaym, and Abd al-Qays as willing submitters, and everyone else as submitting unwillingly.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r3.anchor: وأخرج عن مطر الوراق في الآية قال: الملائكة طوعا والأنصار طوعا وبنو سليم وعبد القيس طوعا

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r4.claim: Qatada says believers submit willingly and benefit from accepted faith, while unbelievers submit only when they see God's punishment, which then avails them nothing; he cites 40:85.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: أما المؤمن فأسلم طائعا

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r5.claim: Al-Hasan specifies the willing submitters as angels in heaven and the Ansar and Abd al-Qays on earth.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في الآية قال: في السماء الملائكة طوعا

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r6.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r6.claim: Al-Sha'bi explains the submission as God's having subjected them.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r6.anchor: وأخرج عن الشعبي {وله أسلم من في السماوات} قال: استقادتهم له

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r7.speaker: أبو سنان
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r7.claim: Abu Sinan glosses submission as recognition: anyone asked knows God.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r7.anchor: وأخرج عن أبي سنان {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض} قال: المعرفة ليس أحد تسأله إلا عرفه

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r8.claim: Ikrima applies unwilling submission to Arab polytheists and captives, including people who entered Islam under compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r8.anchor: وأخرج عن عكرمة في قوله {وكرها} قال: من أسلم من مشركي العرب والسبايا

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r9.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to recite this verse in the ear of ill-tempered enslaved people, animals, or children.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r9.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من ساء خلقه من الرقيق

DURR-FULL:v2p255/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r10.speaker: يونس بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r10.claim: Yunus ibn Ubayd says that reciting the verse in the ear of a difficult mount makes it gentle by God's permission.
DURR-FULL:v2p255/r10.anchor: عن يونس بن عبيد قال: ليس رجل يكون على دابة صعبة فيقرأ في أذنها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies those submitting willingly as the inhabitants of heaven, the Emigrants, the Helpers, and the people of Bahrain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا قال : اهل السموات ، والمهاجرون ، والانصار ، واهل البحرين .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās treats the phrasing as separated and takes the people on earth as submitting willingly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قول الله تعالى : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها قال : هذه مفصولة ومن في الأرض طوعا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the angels in heaven and the Helpers and ʿAbd al-Qays on earth submitted willingly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض قال : في السماء الملائكة طوعا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r4.speaker: عامر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r4.claim: ʿĀmir glosses submission as their being subdued or made subject to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r4.anchor: عن عامر وله اسلم من في السموات قال : استقادتهم له .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r5.speaker: أبو سنان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r5.claim: Abū Sinān interprets willing and unwilling submission as recognition or knowledge of God, saying that anyone asked recognizes Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r5.anchor: ثنا أبي سنان في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها قال : المعرفة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses the phrase as knowledge or recognition.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها قال : المعرفة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says all worship God, willingly or unwillingly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها قال : عبادتهم لي اجمعين طوعا وكرها .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r8.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every human has acknowledged God as Lord and himself as a worshipper; those who sincerely devote themselves do so willingly, while others are compelled.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p695#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والارض طوعا وكرها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the believer prostrates willingly, while the disbeliever prostrates unwillingly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : طوعا وكرها قال : سجود المؤمن طائعا وسجود الكافر وهو كاره .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r2.claim: Qatāda says believers submit willingly, while disbelievers submit when they see God's punishment; faith then cannot benefit them (40:85).
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها قال : اما المؤمن فاسلم طائعا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r3.claim: ʿIkrima takes the first statement as referring to submission by all in heaven and earth, then explains unwilling submission as including Arab polytheists, captives, and those compelled into Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة وله اسلم من في السموات والأرض قال : اسلم من في السموات والأرض ثم استانف طوعا وكرها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says people return to God after life.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p697/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية واليه ترجعون قال : يرجعون اليه بعد الحياة .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو; عاصم; الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yabghūn with yāʾ and turjaʿūn with tāʾ; ʿĀṣim reads both with yāʾ; the others read both with tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: «يبغون» بالياء مفتوحة، و «ترجعون» بالتاء مضمومة، وقرأ عاصم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r4.claim: Most commentators understand aslama here as “submitted.” Min covers all, including angels and both human and jinn peoples.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r4.anchor: وأسلم في هذه الآية بمعنى: استسلم عند جمهور المفسرين، ومن في هذه الآية تعم الملائكة والثقلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid links the verse to 39:38: even disbelievers admit that God created the heavens and earth, so their submission is coerced.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r5.anchor: فقال مجاهد: هذه الآية كقوله تعالى: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r6.speaker: أبو العالية رفيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah says everyone acknowledges God as Lord and themselves as servants: the sincere submit willingly and polytheists submit under compulsion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r6.anchor: وقال بمثل هذا القول أبو العالية رفيع، وعبارته رحمه الله: كل آدمي فقد أقر على نفسه بأن الله ربي وأنا عبده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says reluctant submission took place when the primordial covenant was taken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: بل إسلام الكاره منهم كان حين أخذ الميثاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid also says coercion refers to the disbeliever's shadow prostrating unwillingly, while the believer's shadow prostrates willingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r8.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أنه قال: الكره في هذه الآية هو بسجود ظل الكافر فيسجد المؤمن طوعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r9.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says all humanity submits to God's power even when some assign divinity elsewhere; Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats this as the same basic view as Mujāhid and Abū al-ʿĀliyah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r9.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الآية عبارة عن استقادة جميع البشر لله وإذعانهم لقدرته وإن نسب بعضهم الألوهية إلى غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r10.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says some people accepted Islam willingly and others out of fear of the sword.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: معنى الآية: أنه أسلم قوم طوعا، وأسلم قوم خوف السيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r11.speaker: مطر الوراق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r11.claim: Maṭar al-Warrāq says angels, the Anṣār, Banū Sulaym, and ʿAbd al-Qays submitted willingly; others accepted Islam fearing battle and the sword.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p466#2/r11.anchor: وقال مطر الوراق: أسلمت الملائكة طوعا، وكذلك الأنصار وبنو سليم وعبد القيس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r1.claim: For Maṭar's account, Islam here includes faith; although the wording is universal, its intended sense is particular because some people do not convert this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r1.anchor: وهذا قول الإسلام فيه هو الذي في ضمنه الإيمان، والآية ظاهرها العموم، ومعناها الخصوص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r2.claim: Qatādah says coerced submission is a disbeliever's surrender at death when he sees the truth; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it because this occurs only in a few cases, not with every disbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: الإسلام كرها هو إسلام الكافر عند الموت والمعاينة حيث لا ينفعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r3.claim: The coercion in this argument applies specifically to people on earth; the admonitory question addresses Muḥammad's contemporary scripturalists and disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p467/r3.anchor: والمعنى في هذه الآية، يفهم كل ناظر أن هذا القسم الذي هو الكره إنما هو في أهل الأرض خاصة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو، الباقون، حفص عن عاصم، يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads yabghūn with yāʾ and fatḥa and tarjʿūn with tāʾ and ḍamma; most read yāʾ in both, as does Hafs, who also has fatḥa on yāʾ and kasra on jīm; Yaʿqūb follows his reading in these forms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two scriptural communities disputed over which was closer to Abraham's religion; when the Prophet said neither group followed Abraham's religion, they angrily rejected his judgment and religion, and the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس اختصم أهل الكتابين فزعمت كل فرقة أنها أولى بدين إبراهيم فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r3.claim: The religion of God here means the religion of Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r3.anchor: والمراد بدين الله دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r4.claim: Aslama means submitted and humbled himself.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r5.claim: Ṭawʿan is easy, willing submission; karhan is submission with difficulty and resistance from the self.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r5.anchor: الطوع الانقياد بسهولة والكره الانقياد بمشقة وإباء من النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن مجاهد، الأعمش عن مجاهد، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r6.claim: One of six views says everyone submitted willingly or unwillingly on the day of the primordial covenant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r6.anchor: أحدها أن إسلام الكل كان يوم الميثاق طوعا وكرها رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس والأعمش عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r7.claim: A second view says the believer prostrates willingly while the unbeliever's shadow prostrates unwillingly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r7.anchor: والثاني أن المؤمن يسجد طائعا والكافر يسجد ظله وهو كاره روي عن ابن عباس ورواه ابن أبي نجيح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r8.speaker: أبو العالية، مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r8.claim: A third view says all acknowledge God as Creator; even an associator's acknowledgment is evidence against his shirk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r8.anchor: والثالث أن الكل أقروا له بأنه الخالق وإن أشرك بعضهم فاقراره بذلك حجة عليه في إشراكه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r9.claim: A fourth view says the believer submitted willingly while the unbeliever submitted from fear of the sword.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r9.anchor: الرابع أن المؤمن أسلم طائعا والكافر أسلم مخافة السيف هذا قول الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r10.claim: A fifth view says the unbeliever submitted only upon seeing God's punishment, when submission no longer benefited him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r10.anchor: والخامس أن المؤمن أسلم طائعا والكافر أسلم حين رأى بأس الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r11.speaker: الزجاج، الشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r11.claim: A sixth view says all submit through the nature God created in them; none can resist or change that nature. Al-Zajjaj equates this with al-Shaʿbi's view that all submit to Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p416#3/r11.anchor: والسادس أن إسلام الكل خضوعهم لنفاذ أمره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r1.claim: God rebukes those seeking another religion instead of His revealed religion, which calls people to worship Him alone without partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى منكرا على من أراد دينا سوى دين الله، الذي أنزل به كتبه وأرسل به رسله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r2.claim: Everything in heaven and earth submits to God willingly or unwillingly: believers submit inwardly and outwardly, while unbelievers remain under His irresistible dominion and coercive power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r2.anchor: فالمؤمن مستسلم بقلبه وقالبه لله، والكافر مستسلم لله كرها، فإنه تحت التسخير والقهر والسلطان العظيم، الذي لا يخالف ولا يمانع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links universal submission to verses describing prostration by creation, shadows, animals, and angels, voluntarily or involuntarily and in fear of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} [الرعد:15]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r4.claim: A strange Prophetic interpretation says the heavenly beings are angels, willing earthly submitters are those born Muslim, and unwilling ones are captives from other nations dragged in chains to Paradise; Ibn Kathir prefers the broader submission meaning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r4.anchor: حدثنا الأوزاعي، عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} أما من في السماوات فالملائكة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r5.claim: A report in the Sahih says the Lord marvels at people led to Paradise in chains; Ibn Kathir says he will cite corroboration from another route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r5.anchor: وقد ورد في الصحيح: "عجب ربك من قوم يقادون إلى الجنة في السلاسل"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the willing and unwilling submission as comparable to people acknowledging that God created the heavens and earth when asked.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: هو كقوله: {ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله} [لقمان:25]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains submission as occurring when God took the primordial covenant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p69/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: حين أخذ الميثاق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p70/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p70/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p70/r1.claim: All return to God on the Day of Resurrection, when He recompenses each person according to their deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p70/r1.anchor: {وإليه يرجعون} أي: يوم المعاد، فيجازي كلا بعمله.

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر عن عاصم ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar from ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read both verbs in the third person, linking them to the preceding reference to transgressors.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر عن عاصم ويعقوب (يبغون) و(يرجعون) بالياء فيهما، ردا ذلك إلى قوله: أولئك هم الفاسقون

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads tabghūna in the second person to address Jews and other unbelievers, but yirjiʿūna in the third person for all accountable beings.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو تبغون بالتاء خطابا لليهود وغيرهم من الكفار يرجعون بالياء يرجع إلى جميع المكلفين

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r3.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r3.claim: The other readers use the second person in both verbs, directly addressing the audience.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون فيهما بالتاء على الخطابة قراءة العامة

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r4.speaker: الأعمش
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads karhan with ḍamma on kāf; fatḥa and ḍamma are both dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة كرها بفتح الكاف، وعن الأعمش بضم الكاف، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r5.claim: Baghy originally means seeking; to act unjustly against someone means seeking superiority over him.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r5.anchor: البغي أصله الطلب، بغى يبغي بغيا، وبغى عليه أي يطلب الاستعلاء عليه ظلما

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r6.claim: Someone who obeys has submitted to the command and is its willing subject.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r6.anchor: ويقال: أطاعه إذا انقاد لأمره فهو طوعه

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r7.claim: The two vowelings of karh are valid; one explanation reserves ḍamma for hardship and fatḥa for undertaking an act unwillingly.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r7.anchor: والكره بفتح الكاف وضمها لغتان، وقيل: الكره بالضم المشقة، وبالفتح أن يتكلف الشيء

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r9.claim: The fāʾ coordinates one sentence with another and sequences the question: after these signs, are you seeking another religion? A waw could connect them but lacks that sequence.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r9.anchor: عطف جملة على جملة مثلها، ولو قيل: أوغير جاز إلا أن الفاء ترتب، كأنه قيل: أبعد تلك الآيات

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r10.claim: The alif is interrogative for rebuke or to press the acknowledgment that they do this; another parse attaches it to the verb as a question whether they seek another religion.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r10.anchor: والألف في أفغير ألف الاستفهام، والمراد الإنكار، أو التقرير أنهم يفعلون ذلك

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r11.claim: Ṭawʿan wa-karhan are accusative circumstantial expressions.

JISHUMI:v2p1230/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the People of the Book disputed before the Prophet about Abraham's religion, each group claiming greater entitlement; after he said both were free of Abraham's religion, they rejected his judgment and religion, and the passage was revealed through verse 85.
JISHUMI:v2p1230/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: اختصم أهل الكتاب إلى رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r6.claim: The repudiating hamza is inserted before the coordinating fa; the sense runs, ‘They are wrongdoers—then do they seek a religion other than God’s?’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r6.anchor: دخلت همزة الانكار على الفاء العاطفة جملة على جملة والمعنى فأولئك هم الفاسقون فغير دين الله يبغون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r7.claim: Alternatively, it coordinates with an omitted clause, approximately ‘Do they turn away, then seek a religion other than God’s?’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يعطف على محذوف تقديره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r8.claim: The object ‘other than God’s religion’ is fronted because the denial is directed especially at the false object of worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r8.anchor: وقدم المفعول الذي هو غير دين الله على فعله لأنه اهم من حيث ان الإنكار الذي هو معنى الهمزة متوجه إلى المعبود بالباطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r9.claim: People of the Book disputed before the Prophet over who followed Abraham; he said both groups were clear of Abraham’s religion, and they rejected his judgment and religion, whereupon the verse was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r9.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ( كلا الفريقين بريء من دين إبراهيم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yabghūna with yāʾ and turjaʿūna with tāʾ; both yāʾ forms and both tāʾ forms are also transmitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407/r10.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي عمرو لأن الباغين هم المتولون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r1.claim: Those submit voluntarily by considering the proofs and being fair with themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r1.anchor: بالنظر في الأدلة والإنصاف من نفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r2.claim: Those submit unwillingly under the sword or when confronted by compelling events, such as the mountain over Israel, Pharaoh’s drowning, or imminent death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r2.anchor: بالسيف أو بمعاينة ما يلجىء إلى الإسلام كنتق الجبل على بني اسرائيل وإدراك الغرق فرعون والإشفاء على الموت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r3.claim: The two words are circumstantial accusatives, meaning ‘willing and compelled.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p407#2/r3.anchor: وانتصب طوعا وكرها على الحال بمعنى طائعين ومكرهين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r1.claim: Qatada says believers submit willingly while unbelievers submit unwillingly at death.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r1.anchor: أن المؤمن أسلم طوعا والكافر أسلم عند الموت كرها , وهذا قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets submission as acknowledging servitude, even for someone who associates partners in worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r2.anchor: أنه الإقرار بالعبودية وإن كان فيه من أشرك في العبادة , وهذا قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r3.claim: Another interpretation from Mujahid is that believers prostrate willingly and the shadow of the unbeliever prostrates unwillingly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r3.anchor: أنه سجود المؤمن طائعا وسجود ظل الكافر كرها , وهو مروي عن مجاهد أيضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r4.speaker: مطر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r4.claim: Matar says people submit willingly in hope of reward and unwillingly out of fear of the sword.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r4.anchor: طوعا بالرغبة والثواب . وكرها بالخوف من السيف , وهو قول مطر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets unwilling submission as the acknowledgment people gave when the covenant was taken from them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r5.anchor: أن إسلام الكاره حين أخذ منه الميثاق فأقر به , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r6.speaker: عامر الشعبي، الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r6.claim: Amir al-Shabi and al-Zajjaj understand aslama as submission through compliance and abasement.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p407/r6.anchor: معناه أنه أسلم بالانقياد والذلة , وهو قول عامر الشعبي , والزجاج .

MUJAHID:v1p130#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p130#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p130#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains willing submission as the believer's prostration and unwilling submission as the unbeliever's shadow prostrating while its owner resists.
MUJAHID:v1p130#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ طوعا وكرها ﴾ قال سجود المؤمن طائعا وسجود ظل الكافر وهو كاره

MUQATIL:3:82-83/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:82-83/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:82-83/r2.claim: Those in the heavens who submit willingly are angels; those on earth are believers.

MUQATIL:3:82-83/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:82-83/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:82-83/r3.claim: The reluctant are adherents of other religions: they admit God is their Lord and Creator, yet remain polytheists.
MUQATIL:3:82-83/r3.anchor: يعنى أهل الأديان، يقولون: الله هو ربهم، وهو خلقهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r1.claim: The interrogative rejection follows fāʾ between clauses: «those are the transgressors, so do they seek another religion?»; alternatively it coordinates with an omitted «do they turn away?»
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r1.anchor: دخلت همزة الانكار على الفاء العاطفة جملة على جملة والمعنى فأولئك هم الفاسقون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r2.claim: The object «other than God’s religion» precedes its verb because the rejection targets the false object of worship in particular.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r2.anchor: وقدم المفعول وهو غير دين الله على فعله لأنه أهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r3.claim: Those in heaven are angels; those on earth are humans and jinn.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r4.claim: They submit willingly through reflection on proofs and fairness, or under compulsion by the sword, witnessing punishment, or approaching death.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r4.anchor: بالنظر فى الأدلة والإنصاف من نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r5.claim: «Willingly and unwillingly» is adverbial, describing submission in either state.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r5.anchor: وانتصب طوعا وكرها على الحال أى طائعين ومكرهين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r6.speaker: حفص وأبو عمرو وسائر القراء
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r6.claim: Ḥafṣ reads both verbs with yāʾ; Abū ʿAmr reads the second with tāʾ and fatḥa on its jīm; the others read both with tāʾ and that fatḥa.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r6.anchor: يبغون ويرجعون بالياء فيهما حفص وبالتاء فى الثاني وفتح الجيم أبو عمرو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r7.claim: The transgressors are those seeking another religion, but all people return to God for recompense.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p164#3/r7.anchor: لأن الباغين هم المتولون والراجعون جميع الناس

BURSEVI:v2p45/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r3.claim: Since the covenant was in their scriptures and they knew Muhammad's prophethood was true, only enmity and envy explain their disbelief; like Iblis, they seek a religion other than God's.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r3.anchor: فقد كانوا عالمين بصدق محمد عليه السلام في النبوة فلم يبق لكفرهم سبب إلا مجرد العداوة والحسد

BURSEVI:v2p45/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r4.claim: The question coordinates with an understood clause: do they turn away and then seek a religion other than God's?
BURSEVI:v2p45/r4.anchor: عطف على مقدر أي أيتولون فيبغون غير دين الله ويطلبونه

BURSEVI:v2p45/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r5.claim: Aslama means to submit sincerely and yield; those in heaven and earth means their inhabitants.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r5.anchor: أخلص وانقاد {من فى السماوات والارض} أي أهلهما

BURSEVI:v2p45/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r6.claim: Those who submit willingly are monotheists; deniers submit unwillingly through creation's signs, bodily changes, illness and health, wealth and poverty, joy and grief, and other states under God's decree.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r6.anchor: وهم الموحدون {وكرها} أي بإباء وهم الجاحدون

BURSEVI:v2p45/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r7.claim: All inhabitants return to God, warning rejecters of the true religion that none besides Him can bring harm or benefit.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r7.anchor: أي من فيهما والمراد أن من خالفه في العاجل فسيكون مرجعه إليه من حيث لا يملك الضر والنفع

BURSEVI:v2p45/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r8.claim: A rational person should obey God rather than break the covenant made on the primordial day.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r8.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يطيع ربه ولا يعصيه بنقض ما عهد إليه يوم الميثاق

BURSEVI:v2p45/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p45/r9.claim: The covenant with prophets, saints, and believers is to affirm God's oneness, uphold religion without division, confirm one another, call people to obedience, and reserve worship for God; He asks sincere servitude and fulfillment of the Lord's rights.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r9.anchor: فعهد الله مع الأنبياء والأولياء والمؤمنين التوحيد وإقامة الدين وعدم التفرق فيه وتصديق بعضهم بعضا

BURSEVI:v2p45/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p45/r10.speaker: الشيخ الشاذلي
BURSEVI:v2p45/r10.claim: Al-Shadhili says it is an evident blessing when God grants obedience and then effaces the servant's awareness of it, relieving the outward self from disobeying Him.
BURSEVI:v2p45/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ الشاذلي قدس سره : متى رزقك الله الطاعة والفناء به عنها فقد أسبغ عليك نعمة ظاهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r1.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and his companions disputed with Christians before the Prophet over Abraham’s religion; they rejected his judgment and faith, prompting the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: إن كعب بن الأشرف وأصحابه اختصموا مع النصارى إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r3.claim: غير is accusative as the object of يبغون: they seek a religion other than God’s.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r3.anchor: ونصبت «غير» بيبغون، أي يبغون غير دين الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads يبغون in the third person but ترجعون in the second, distinguishing the specific first clause from the general second.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده «يبغون» بالياء على الخبر «وإليه ترجعون» بالتاء على المخاطبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r5.speaker: حفص وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ and others read both verbs in the third person, connected to “those are the defiantly disobedient.”
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r5.anchor: وقرأ حفص وغيره «يبغون، ويرجعون» بالياء فيهما لقوله: { فأولئك هم الفاسقون }.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r6.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r6.claim: The remaining readers use the second person for both verbs, matching the address in 3:81.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما على الخطاب لقوله لمآ آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r7.claim: أسلم means submitted, obeyed, yielded, and humbled oneself.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r8.claim: Every creature is subject because each is made with a nature it cannot escape.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r8.anchor: وكل مخلوق فهو منقاد مستسلم لأنه مجبول على ما لا يقدر أن يخرج عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r9.claim: Qatāda says believers submit willingly, while unbelievers submit under compulsion at death, which does not benefit them; he cites 40:85.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: أسلم المؤمن طوعا والكافر عند موته كرها ولا ينفعه ذلك لقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains coerced submission by an unbeliever prostrating to another deity while his shadow prostrates to God, as in 16:48.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد: إسلام الكافر كرها بسجوده لغير الله وسجود ظله لله،

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r11.claim: The shadow’s prostration is also linked to 13:15, which says shadows prostrate willingly and unwillingly.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r11.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r12.claim: Another explanation is that God made varied people and all are compelled to submit: the healthy gladly, the sick reluctantly.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r12.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أن الله خلق الخلق على ما أراد منهم فمنهم الحسن والقبيح والطويل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r13.claim: طوع is easy willing compliance; كره is compliance with difficulty and inner resistance.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r13.anchor: والطوع الانقياد والاتباع بسهولة. والكره ما كان بمشقة وإباء من النفس.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r14.claim: طوعا and كرها are verbal nouns functioning circumstantially, meaning willingly and unwillingly.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84/r14.anchor: و { طوعا وكرها } مصدران في موضع الحال، أي طائعين ومكرهين.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r1.claim: The continuation of the cited Prophetic report says the angels obeyed in heaven and the Anṣār and ʿAbd al-Qays on earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r2.claim: The Prophet forbids insulting his Companions, saying they submitted from fear of God while other people submitted from fear of the sword.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r2.anchor:
وقال عليه السلام:
" لا تسبوا أصحابي فإن أصحابي أسلموا من خوف الله وأسلم الناس من خوف السيف "

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says voluntary submission is accepting Islam without disputation, while coerced submission is being compelled to monotheism by argument; he cites 43:87 and 29:61.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة: «طوعا» من أسلم من غير محاجة «وكرها» من اضطرته الحجة إلى التوحيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan calls the wording general but its intended referent particular.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: هو عموم معناه الخصوص.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan treats “those in the heavens have submitted” as a complete clause, then begins a new clause about the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r5.anchor: وعنه: { أسلم من في السماوات } وتم الكلام. ثم قال: { والأرض طوعا وكرها }.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the reluctant hypocrite gains no benefit from his deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r6.anchor: قال: والكاره المنافق لا ينفعه عمله.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās a recommendation to recite this verse into the ear of a stubborn or difficult riding animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:83-84#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: إذا استصعبت دابة أحدكم أو كانت شموسا فليقرأ فى أذنها هذه الآية:

RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r1.claim: Since the preceding verse makes belief in Muhammad obligatory by God's covenant with earlier prophets and peoples, those who reject him seek a religion other than God's.
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r1.anchor: لما بين في الآية الأولى أن الإيمان بمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام شرع شرعه الله وأوجبه على جميع من مضى من الأنبياء والأمم

RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads both verbs in the third person, connecting the first to the defiant people in 3:82 and the second to the Jews and Christians under discussion.
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم { يبغون } و { يرجعون } بالياء المنقطة من تحتها

RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the first verb as second-person address to the Jews and other disbelievers, but keeps the final verb third-person for all accountable people mentioned in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو { * تبغون } بالتاء خطابا لليهود وغيرهم من الكافر و { لا يرجعون } بالياء

RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r4.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r4.claim: The remaining readers use second-person address in both verbs, matching the preceding direct address and potentially addressing everyone, believers and disbelievers alike.
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون فيهما بالتاء على الخطاب ، لأن ما قبله خطاب كقوله { ءأقررتم وأخذتم }

RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r5.claim: The interrogative rebukes or confirms their seeking; it is grammatically directed at the verb, while the object is fronted because the rejection targets the false object of worship, and the fa links clauses.
RAZI-FULL:v8p106#2/r5.anchor: الهمزة للاستفهام والمراد استنكار أن يفعلوا ذلك أو تقرير أنهم يفعلونه ، وموضع الهمزة هو لفظة { يبغون }

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r1.claim: Although a waw could replace the fa, the fa adds the sense: after this emphatically confirmed covenant, do you still seek another religion?
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه لو قيل أو غير دين الله يبغون جاز إلا أن في الفاء فائدة زائدة كأنه قيل : أفبعد أخذ هذا الميثاق المؤكد

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r2.speaker: روي
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r2.claim: A report says two groups of People of the Book disputed before the Prophet over which group followed Abraham's religion; he declared both disavowed from it, and they rejected his judgment and religion, whereupon the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r2.anchor: روي أن فريقين من أهل الكتاب اختصموا إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما اختلفوا فيه من دين إبراهيم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that occasion because it disconnects the verse from its context, whereas the rebuke-question requires a link to what precedes.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r3.anchor: ويبعد عندي حمل هذه الآية على هذا السبب لأن على هذا التقدير تكون هذه الآية منقطعة عما قبلها ، والاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار يقتضي تعلقها بما قبلها

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r4.claim: Their scriptures contained the covenant, so they knew Muhammad's prophethood was true; envy and hostility alone explain their unbelief, like Iblīs, and seeking another religion and disobeying God is irrational.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r4.anchor: هذا الميثاق لما كان مذكورا في كتبهم وهم كانوا عارفين بذلك فقد كانوا عالمين بصدق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في النبوة فلم يبق لكفرهم سبب إلا مجرد العداوة والحسد

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r5.claim: Islam here means surrender, obedience, and submission.

RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r6.claim: The strongest reading is that everything besides God is possible in itself and depends on God both to exist and to cease; thus all creation submits in both states, and the exclusive to Him affirms one necessary existent and God's sole creative power over every kind of being.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107/r6.anchor: وهو الأصح عندي أن كل ما سوى الله سبحانه ممكن لذاته وكل ممكن لذاته فإنه لا يوجد إلا بإيجاده ولا يعدم إلا بإعدامه

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r1.claim: The strongest account says no one can resist God's will: righteous people obey religious duties willingly but endure illness, poverty, and death unwillingly; unbelievers submit unwillingly in other matters.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r1.anchor: لا سبيل لأحد إلى الامتناع عليه في مراده ، وإما أن ينزلوا عليه طوعا أو كرها ، فالمسلمون الصالحون ينقادون لله طوعا فيما يتعلق بالدين

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r2.claim: Another view says Muslims submit willingly, while unbelievers submit unwillingly at death.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r2.anchor: أسلم المسلمون طوعا ، والكافرون عند موتهم كرها لقوله تعالى : { فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا }

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r3.claim: All people acknowledge God's divinity willingly, as shown by their answer that God created the heavens and earth, but accept obligations and painful creation unwillingly.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r3.anchor: أن كل الخلق منقادون لإلاهيته طوعا بدليل قوله تعالى : { ولئن سألتهم من خلق * السماوات والارض ليقولن الله }

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation places universal submission at the primordial covenant, when Adam's descendants affirmed God's lordship.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r4.anchor: أن انقياد الكل إنما حصل وقت أخذ الميثاق وهو قوله تعالى : { وإذ أخذ ربك من بنىءادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى }

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the heavenly beings submit willingly, while among earthly beings some submit willingly and others unwillingly.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسن : الطوع لأهل السماوات خاصة ، وأما أهل الأرض فبعضهم بالطوع وبعضهم بالكره

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī connects this contrast with God's command to heaven and earth to come willingly or unwillingly; both answer that they come willingly, a passage he says contains wondrous secrets.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r6.anchor: وأقول : إنه سبحانه ذكر في تخليق السماوات والأرض هذا وهو قوله { فقال لها وللارض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين }

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r7.claim: Those who oppose God in this life return to Him, where no one else can cause harm or benefit; this is a grave warning to rejecters of the true religion.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r7.anchor: من خالفه في العاجل فسيكون مرجعه إليه ، والمراد إلى حيث لا يملك الضر والنفع سواه هذا وعيد عظيم لمن خالف الدين الحق

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines ṭawʿ as compliance and submission, with related verbs meaning obey, comply with, or agree.

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r9.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt notes that Arabic uses both ṭāʿa lahu and aṭāʿa for obeying.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : يقال طاع له وأطاع ، فانتصب طوعا وكرها على أنه مصدر وقع موقع الحال

RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r10.claim: The accusative ṭawʿan wa-karhan is a verbal noun used circumstantially, equivalent to willing compliance or unwilling compliance; one cannot use speech to mean speaking as a manner of arrival.
RAZI-FULL:v8p107#2/r10.anchor: تقديره طائعا وكارها ، كقولك أتاني راكضا
